title: Squares of effective lines on semiabelian varieties are globally generated
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $J\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite presentation [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Its addition, inverse and identity are morphisms over $k$ satisfying the commutative group identities; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Assume $J$ is geometrically semiabelian, that is, this structure morphism has semiabelian geometric fibres [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres]. Let $C$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_J$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] with a nonzero global section $s\in\Gamma(J,C)$. Then $C^{\otimes2}=C\otimes_{\mathcal O_J}C$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] is generated by global sections [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]. Equivalently, there is a finite family of global sections of $C^{\otimes2}$ whose values span its one-dimensional residue-field fibre at every point of $J$. No ampleness, symmetry, properness or algebraic closedness assumption is made.

source.place: I 2.6, relative theorem of the cube, followed by the translation argument for an effective line; original local WANTED. Agent-extracted field lemma. proof.text: Choose an algebraically closed extension $K/k$ for which $J_K$ is Jacobson and all its closed points are $K$-rational, by [lem-sfb-scheme-large-algclosed-jacobson]. Write $H=J_K$, $L=C_K$, and $p:H\to J$. The group operations base change termwise, preserving their identities. Smoothness follows from [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), separatedness from [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change], and finite presentation from [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). In particular $J$ and $H$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, as finite presentation includes these conditions [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. By [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres], $H$ is an extension of an abelian variety by a split torus, so [lem-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-power-integrality] with $n=1$ makes $H$ integral. Pullback preserves invertible modules by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](1).

source.place: Tag 0479, lemma-make-Jacobson; geometric group integrality as in groupoids.tex Tag 0B7Q; base-change inputs cited individually

proof.text: The field extension is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] with $D=k$. Since $C$ is quasi-coherent by [def-sc-invertible-module], degree zero of [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] gives $\Gamma(J,C)\otimes_k K\simeq\Gamma(H,L)$ by $t\otimes a\mapsto a p^*t$. Thus $u=p^*s\ne0$: extending a $k$-basis containing $s$ shows $s\otimes1\ne0$. Let $V=H_u$. It is open by [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes] and is nonempty: choose a nonempty affine trivializing open on which $u$ has nonzero coefficient $f$. Its coordinate ring is a domain, since $H$ is integral; the zero prime belongs to $D(f)\subset V$.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology (2), i=0; modules.tex Tag 01CY, lemma-s-open; elementary domain calculation for nonemptiness

proof.text:
Choose a basis of the one-dimensional $K$-space $e^*L$, giving a rigidification. Apply [lem-sfb-semiabelian-cubical-rigidification](b): $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is normal since its sole local ring is a field, and $H$ is geometrically connected because all its geometric fibres are semiabelian and integral by [lem-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-power-integrality]. Pull back the trivial cube line in [def-sfb-cubical-rigidified-line] along $H\to H^3$, $z\mapsto(z,a,-a)$, for $a\in H(K)$. Writing $t_a(z)=z+a$, its factors are
$$L^{\otimes2}\otimes\underline{L(a)}\otimes\underline{L(-a)}\otimes(t_a^*L)^{\vee}\otimes(t_{-a}^*L)^{\vee}\otimes\underline{L(e)}^{\vee\otimes2}.$$
Here underlining means the constant invertible module associated to the indicated one-dimensional $K$-space. Each constant factor is trivial after choosing a basis. The pullback, tensor and composition identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](2) therefore give an isomorphism $t_a^*L\otimes t_{-a}^*L\simeq L^{\otimes2}$. No symmetry of $L$ is used.

source.place: I Corollary 5.3, printed p.22, substitution (z,a,-a); semiabelian cube supplied by the cited node, cross-checked in Lan revised thesis Proposition 3.2.3.1(2), printed p.68

proof.text: Fix any closed point $x\in H$; it is $K$-rational by [lem-sfb-scheme-large-algclosed-jacobson]. The maps $a\mapsto x+a$ and $a\mapsto x-a$ are automorphisms, with inverses $z\mapsto z-x$ and $z\mapsto x-z$. Their inverse images of $V$ are nonempty open subsets of the irreducible scheme $H$ [lem-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-power-integrality]. Their intersection is nonempty and contains a closed, hence $K$-rational, point $a$, by the density assertion of [lem-sfb-scheme-large-algclosed-jacobson]. Consequently $u(x+a)\ne0$ and $u(x-a)\ne0$. The section $t_a^*u\otimes t_{-a}^*u$ has nonzero value at $x$ by the fibre formula of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](3); a tensor of two nonzero vectors in one-dimensional spaces over a field is nonzero. Transporting it along the isomorphism in step 3 produces $v_x\in\Gamma(H,L^{\otimes2})$ nonzero at $x$.

source.place: I Theorem 5.5 and Remark 5.6, printed p.23, translation identity; agent translation/nonvanishing argument using the semiabelian cube instead of abelian properness

proof.text: The union of the nonvanishing opens $H_v$ over all $v\in\Gamma(H,L^{\otimes2})$ contains every closed point by step 4. These loci are open by [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes]. Its closed complement must be empty by [lem-sfb-scheme-large-algclosed-jacobson](i), which gives density of closed points in every closed subset. Now let $y\in J$. The map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is surjective (both spaces have one point), so [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] supplies $z\in H$ over $y$. Choose $v$ with $v(z)\ne0$. The line $C^{\otimes2}$ is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](1), hence quasi-coherent. Apply [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] in degree zero to this line. Together with its tensor-pullback identification [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](2), it writes $v=\sum_{i=1}^r a_i p^*w_i$, with $a_i\in K$ and $w_i\in\Gamma(J,C^{\otimes2})$. If every $w_i(y)$ were zero, the fibre formula [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](3) would make $v(z)=0$. Thus some $w_i(y)\ne0$. This proves the nonvanishing opens of global sections of $C^{\otimes2}$ cover $J$.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, i=0; modules.tex Tag 01CY; varieties.tex Tag 0479; elementary descent of nonzero evaluations by finite tensor expressions

proof.text: The nonvanishing loci just constructed are open by [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes]. Since $J$ is quasi-compact, the definition [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] gives finitely many such sections covering $J$. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-generating-sections-fibre] this finite family generates $C^{\otimes2}$, and the same criterion gives the stated residue-field-fibre formulation.

I checked every cited statement against its use. Step 1: J_K is integral by the large-field Jacobson node (i)/(ii), smooth/separated/finite-presentation base change, and power-integrality with n=1 (B is an abelian variety, so proper, smooth and connected over K̄). Step 2: degree-0 flat base change gives p*s≠0; H_u is nonempty because H is integral (a domain coefficient, the generic point lies in D(f)). Step 3: I recomputed all 8 factors of Θ_3 pulled back along (z,a,−a), including the two L(e)^∨ factors; rigidification(b) applies over the normal base Spec K with geometrically integral fibres; this gives t_a*L⊗t_{-a}*L≅L^2. Step 4: the two preimages meet by irreducibility, closed points are dense and K-rational, and the fibre formula gives a section nonzero at x. Step 5: density in every closed subset gives all points; then surjective base change plus flat base change v=Σa_i p*w_i descend generation (valid for finite and imperfect k). Step 6: elementary qc finite subcover plus the generating-sections fibre criterion. Source: Milne AV I Cor 5.3/Thm 5.5 pp.22-23, read locally; same substitution. No SGA. Duplicate search (semiabelian, square, t_a, globally generated): picard-square-triviality, cubical-symmetric-multiplication-square and translation-difference-surjectivity are different statements. Small cases: Spec k, G_m^r, abelian, char 2, finite k.
